overclaim_search_hits.text: The M4 runtime estimator first takes each condition's median of \RTReps\ repetitions, then forms a prompt latency ratio and its geometric mean across \RTPrompts\ prompts. The offline oracle uses the smaller target-only or Always-Spec median for each prompt. Bootstrap intervals use \RTBootstrap\ draws with Python Random seed \RTSeed, resampling prompts in the frozen held-out order. Percentile endpoints linearly interpolate the sorted bootstrap draws at quantiles .025 and .975. A single random stream computes Target/Guard, Target/Always-Spec, and Guard/oracle intervals in that order. This preserves the frozen finite-bootstrap calculation; it does not replace the hardware estimators in Table~\ref{tab:statistics}. Intervals condition on the selected policy and observed prompt medians; they do not incorporate recalibration or between-session variation. The oracle selects between two measured fixed conditions, not all possible switching policies, so it is not a universal latency lower bound.

Calibration, qualification, and held-out IDs are disjoint. Selection ranks tasks with no recorded prior M4 exposure in the frozen inventory by a seeded hash within each of HumanEval and Spec-Bench; each split is balanced across these two families. The registered grid has nine candidates: first decision round $E\in\{2,4,8\}$ and margin $m\in\{0,0.05,0.10\}$. Calibration selects the exact candidate with the lowest geometric-mean latency ratio to the offline oracle. Exact ties break by mean measured guard-compute overhead, smaller exploration count, larger margin, and lexicographic candidate ID. The frozen winner is \texttt{E8\_M000}; held-out results never select or retune it.

Table~\ref{tab:directidqualification} reports new studies separately from the historical context lookup and timing inventory. Both freeze the same HumanEval30 IDs, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-0.6B Q8\_0 models, greedy $k=2$, three repetitions, cap 128, and a 90/90 sequence-equality rule. Prompt IDs and uncommitted proposals are excluded; an earlier generated terminal EOG is included. No mismatch is discarded and no subset qualifies. Historical path-control outcomes informed the replications; prospective freezing does not imply blinded discovery. Each study completes 270 executions; independent offline implementations reproduce all 180 comparisons, including first divergences. Operational elapsed fields do not establish formal performance.

B570 uses source instrumentation to record committed IDs in sidecars, context 1024, and a separately frozen completion reference. Its endpoint selects the first 128 committed IDs or the inclusive earlier EOG; raw CLI overshoot is retained. Vulkan0 uses driver 32.0.101.9033 with full target 37/37 and draft 29/29 layer offload. The initial Task Scheduler launch failed during CP936/UTF-8 environment-metadata decoding before inference, with zero formal executions. The first data-producing attempt directly ran the unchanged frozen runner: no semantic, code, binary, model, driver, or parameter change occurred. This deployment deviation is preserved in provenance.

The 24 reserved IDs are HumanEval/58, 156, 134, 42, 122, 114, 93, 115, 151, 63, 125, 133, 43, 139, 77, 35, 27, 34, 145, 82, 154, 78, 96, and 138. Target reference and target-only predictor run three times each (144 executions) with within-condition repeat stability. All 72 predicted complete ID arrays and their digest are committed before the first of 72 live serialized outcomes. Primary success requires 72/72 complete predictor-to-live sequences; no partial threshold or confidence interval is substituted. Prediction matches 72/72. Twenty prompts are predicted reference-equal; four are predicted divergent, and all 24 classifications match. Among the 12 divergent repetition pairs, the first-divergence index matches 12/12. Those four prompts and zero-based indices (reference token $\rightarrow$ serialized token) are HumanEval/134: 88 (914$\rightarrow$1946); /42: 73 (432$\rightarrow$1817); /145: 103 (1184$\rightarrow$686); and /138: 93 (14374$\rightarrow$9064). Predicted and actual reference equality is 60/72, blocked on this reserved set.

The v0.7 B570 residual could reflect reference, front-end, context, or target-partition differences. A target-only harness first reproduces 90/90 reference sequences. On 12 outcome-exposed discovery prompts, target-only greedy execution with $n_{\mathrm{ubatch}}=1$ matches 36/36 serialized speculative sequences. The frozen H1/H2 decision tree selects H1 (target-partition sufficiency); H2 is not run. Discovery is exploratory.

An exposure audit conservatively excludes 31 tasks, then deterministically selects 24 reserved HumanEval prompts from 133 eligible tasks. H1 is committed before reserved inference; all 72 complete target-only predictions are committed before any live serialized outcome. The live runs match 72/72 predicted sequences, 24/24 prompt classifications, and 12/12 divergent repetition-pair first-divergence indices across four prompts. Predicted and actual reference equality is 60/72, so qualification remains \emph{blocked}. No parameter or prediction changes after their respective freezes; no selective reruns occur. The appendix gives task IDs, divergence tokens, and audit scope.

Historical RTX and B570 controls first identified a verification-path qualification issue. Two subsequent prospectively frozen direct-ID studies share HumanEval30 task IDs, the Qwen3-8B/0.6B Q8\_0 model pair, greedy $k=2$, three repetitions, and a 90/90 qualification rule. RTX agreement changes from \DIRTXBatchedPairs/90 batched pairs to \DIRTXSerializedPairs/90 serialized pairs; B570 changes from \DIBFastPairs/90 to \DIBSerializedPairs/90 and remains blocked. A controlled B570 follow-up isolates target execution partition as a sufficient predictor of the serialized output trajectory: target-only micro-batch one matches 36/36 exposed discovery sequences, then predicts 72/72 complete sequences on a separately frozen reserved set. On 358H, the isolated NPU draft advantage does not survive the tested stateful integration, while complete target-side work dominates CPU drafting. All timing gains concern post-prefill decode, excluding loading and initial prompt prefill.

RTX serialization crosses the 90/90 gate, while B570 serialization improves agreement without crossing it. First qualify the intended path against its output contract. If it fails, isolate the target partition before assigning the failure to live drafting or device placement. Only then use complete realized cost to assess profitability on a qualified path. This evidence-derived sequence is bounded by the tested configurations. The separately frozen runtime studies on different stacks are not an intervention/ablation chain.

The strict output contract is conditional on the frozen reference; another quality objective could admit other paths. Historical M4, RTX, and B570 equality counts use re-tokenized CLI text, with campaign-specific parsing. They cannot establish direct generated-ID equality; the historical labels and counts remain evidence of their recorded comparator only. Two fresh RTX/B570 studies supply direct generated-ID evidence without retroactively certifying historical timing. They cover one model pair, HumanEval30, fixed $k=2$, and three repetitions; differing runtime/reference/context settings prevent estimating a causal hardware difference. The fresh RTX driver is 616.92 versus historical 616.56. B570 launcher recovery changes deployment, not frozen study semantics. The follow-up H1 predictor covers one B570 platform, model pair, runtime/build, greedy $k=2$, HumanEval workload, and 24 reserved prompts. ``No known B570 exposure'' means no record in the audited scope, not proof that a task was never run. Target partition is sufficient to reproduce these trajectories, but the study neither identifies a specific kernel nor proves an architecture-wide cause, a CUDA/B570 common mechanism, or a universal micro-batch rule. The predictor is explanatory evidence, not a production certificate. Prompt counts do not establish backend-wide behavior. HumanEval functional execution and pass@$k$ were not evaluated. CUDA/B570 and the 358H runtime qualification findings concern their tested paths, not general backend unsuitability. Replay and proposal share one timed region, so their individual causal costs and a persistence benefit are not established. The 358H intervention did not reach formal performance evaluation.

The reference is the median across calibration prompts of each prompt's median target latency divided by its median output-token count. The preregistered candidate grid varies the first decision round and margin. Selection minimizes calibration geometric-mean latency relative to the offline minimum of target-only and Always-Spec among exact candidates, with frozen tie-breaks. The selected rule uses margin \RTMargin\ and first decides after \RTRounds\ completed speculative rounds; it then decides after each later round while speculation continues. A request ending earlier makes no decision. The online policy receives neither task/family labels nor future output length, current-request target-only latency, or oracle outcomes.

\caption{M4 per-prompt median post-prefill latencies. Each speculative condition is \RTExact/\RTExact\ direct-token exact. The first two rows report speedups. The offline oracle uses the lower target-only or Always-Spec median and is unavailable online; its row reports latency regret. The separated Guard/Always-Spec contrast is reviewer-requested post-study paired secondary analysis; values above one mean Guard is slower.}
